items.title: The Hilbert function of a finite graded module is a numerical polynomial in degree one
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition states that for a Noetherian graded ring with the positive part generated in degree one and a finite graded module, the function recording the class of the n-th graded piece is a numerical polynomial (statement lines 14106-14118). The proof does not compute Hilbert series: it inducts on the minimal number of degree-one generators, and in the induction step compares the graded pieces of the module with those of the quotient by the chosen generator, concluding by the numerical polynomial criterion (proof lines 14120-14161). Setting up the induction on that generator count is the step that makes the comparison finite. H2.
